impact:
Scope boundary declared explicitly in T-005 rather than silently left open (plan section 3.5).

T-005 validates that every waiver a comparison policy consumes names a published ALLOWLIST entry, and that each policy actually executes its replacement assertions (proved by mutation-killing every predicate). That covers ALLOWLIST-19, -22b and -23.

What it deliberately does NOT cover: entries asserted by tests that are not parity cases — ALLOWLIST-22a (the product-name spans, asserted by the reviewed shipped-help snapshot) being the live example. An earlier plan revision proposed classifying such entries "enforceable" by listing their asserting test NAMES. Review correctly rejected that: the existence of a test name is exactly the "code exists, therefore it ran" evidence this repo removed dual_run_only to escape. Naming it proves nothing.

Doing it properly needs a runner that REPORTS which allowlist IDs actually executed — a machine-readable assertion registry, where a test declares the ID it asserts and the runner emits the set that ran, so coverage is computed from execution rather than from prose.

Until that exists, ALLOWLIST-22a is documented as snapshot-asserted and is not machine-verified. That is a stated gap, not a claim of coverage. Related: ALLOWLIST entry 22 was split into 22a/22b during T-005 precisely so the documentation-only half could not shelter the enforced half.
title: Allowlist IDs asserted by NON-CASE tests have no execution evidence
